hero.title: Your health data belongs to [[you]]. Not the cloud.
hero.sub: Trota is a women's health chatbot built around you. Ask questions, bring your data from other health apps, and get answers with sources. Your records stay on your phone, and you decide what happens to them.
hero.q: I get headaches before my period. Is that normal?
hero.a: Common, and often linked to hormone shifts. Your log shows it starting about two days before each period. If it gets worse, see a doctor.
hero.work: Checking your record and the library…
hero.foot: Names and numbers removed before anything is sent

about.title: Meet Trota
about.p1: Trota is a women's health chatbot. Ask it what you'd normally type into a search engine and get plain-language answers, with sources you can check.
about.p2: Bring your data from other health apps if you like. It stays on your phone, and a small local engine learns your patterns so answers fit you.
about.p3: Your data is yours. You choose what happens to it, and you can change your mind at any time.

sec.title: Security
sec.lead: Code on your phone decides what the AI can see.
sec.d0: Your question is read on your phone. Nothing has left it yet.
sec.x0: In a standard setup the question goes straight to a cloud model, name included.
sec.d1: Before any searching happens, a plain database rule decides which of your records this question may touch. Everything else is never loaded.
sec.x1: No limits are applied, so all 1,284 entries could be retrieved.
sec.d2: Your records and the medical library live in separate stores. Search runs on the records that passed the filter, and on the library separately.
sec.x2: Records and public text sit in one pool and are searched together.
sec.d3: Regex and word lists find names, numbers and instruction-like text, and replace them before anything is sent.
sec.x3: No cleaning step, so the model sees the name, the ID and any hidden text in the file.
sec.d4: The cloud AI receives a cleaned question and a small set of cleaned facts. It writes the answer. It never sees the rest.
sec.x4: Everything retrieved is sent as written.
sec.q: I'm Savi Fernando, 29. My cycle has been irregular since March. Should I be worried?
sec.n0y: Still on your phone. Nothing has been sent.
sec.n0x: Sent as typed, with your name.
sec.fTyp: No limits: every entry can be reached.
sec.mSim: Similarity search runs only on the {n} allowed records.
sec.mPile: One pile, searched together. Nothing keeps your records apart.
sec.cFoundT: Nothing cleaned. This is sent as is.
sec.cAtk: Even if a line like this slipped through, the AI could only ever see the {n} allowed records.
more: Retrieval is filter-then-search. An SQL WHERE clause (user, category, date range) narrows the records first, and vector similarity runs only on what's left. Out-of-bounds records are never loaded into memory.
Your records and the medical library are separate stores.

Before anything is sent, a regex and dictionary sanitizer replaces names, IDs, phone numbers, addresses and instruction-like text from imported files. This stops hidden instructions in a file from reaching the model.
Backups are encrypted snapshots. The cloud only ever stores ciphertext.

src.title: Sourced answers
src.lead: Every passage is indexed by provenance: where it came from, who published it and who checked it.
src.q: Why do I get headaches before my period?
src.c2: They are often linked to hormone shifts.
src.c3: If they get worse, a doctor can check.
src.hint: Tap a claim to follow it back to its source.
src.passage: The exact passage, saved with its page reference
src.noneNote: Without an index, a claim can't be traced back.
more: Every passage is stored with its provenance: source document, page, publisher, how it was verified, and the date and version it was added.
The model is given passages with their IDs and has to cite them. Claims without a matching passage are removed before you see the answer.
The library is limited to peer-reviewed papers, verified journals and public professional profiles. Web pages and forums aren't included.

eng.title: Who does what
eng.lead: Every question is split. Code handles what can be calculated. AI handles the wording.
eng.detD: Same input, same result. Finds, counts, checks.
eng.probD: Writes in plain language. Wording can vary.

p1.q: Has my cycle been getting longer?
p1.c2: Work out the usual length and trend
p1.pk: 2 facts: usual length, latest three cycles
p1.ans: Your last three cycles were [[34, 36 and 35 days]], longer than your usual [[31 days]]. Cycles can drift for many reasons. If it keeps going, mention it to a doctor.

p2.q: Why do I get headaches before my period?
p2.ans: Your log shows headaches in [[6 of your last 8 cycles]], usually about [[2 days]] before your period. Research links this to hormone shifts [1]. If it gets worse, see a doctor.

p3.q: Explain my last cycle in Sinhala.
p3.ans: ඔබේ අවසන් චක්‍රය [[දින 36]] ක් විය, ඔබේ සාමාන්‍යයට වඩා [[දින 5]] ක් දිගයි.

eng.mNote: Illustrative: about 700 tokens per month of raw logs, a 16,000-token window.
more: We follow the Rule of Least Power: use the simplest tool that can do the job. Parsing, filtering, counting and redaction are plain code, so they behave the same way every time and can't be talked out of their rules.
The model gets a short packet of facts and source passages instead of your raw history, which keeps token use and response time down.
Numbers in an answer come from code, not from the model. The model only writes the sentences around them, in English, Sinhala or Tamil.

trk.title: Your tracker
trk.lead: Plain statistics and data structures, no AI. Each entry updates them in one step.
trk.ringD: A fixed-size list of the latest.
trk.adaptD: Reacts faster when your pattern shifts. Weight {a}.
trk.fcD: Narrows when your pattern is steady, widens when it isn't.
trk.evOk: Entry {i}: {v} days. In line with your pattern.
trk.evFlag: Entry {i}: {v} days stands out from your pattern.
more: Welford's algorithm keeps a running mean and variance, updated in one step per entry.
A fixed-size ring buffer holds recent entries and a hash map holds frequency counts. Both update in constant time.
An exponentially weighted average follows recent change. Its weight rises when your pattern gets more variable, so it reacts faster.
Entries more than two standard deviations from your pattern are flagged. The forecast is a 95% prediction interval that narrows as more data comes in.

imp.title: Who it helps
imp.youB: Plain-language answers with sources you can check.
imp.docH: A fuller history in the room
imp.docB: A report built from your own entries: patterns, changes and flagged shifts, ready to bring to an appointment.
imp.resB: Opt-in, de-identified entries can build long-term datasets for women's health. Researchers can also reuse the tracking engine.
imp.indB: Code enforces limits, a closed library backs every claim, and people stay in charge. Medical AI as a tool, not a replacement.
imp.pa: The years before periods stop, when hormone levels shift. Symptoms vary a lot from person to person.
imp.k2: Sensitive details removed before the cloud
imp.k5: Clinicians and users make the decisions

footer.ethics: Trota gives general health information, not a diagnosis. Please talk to a doctor about any health decision.

journey.title: Follow our journey
journey.thanks: Thank you. You are on the list.
journey.lead: Updates as we build, and a say in what comes next.

inp.title: Bring your data
inp.lead: Import from the apps you already use. Update when you want, and stay in charge.
inp.rangeNote: Illustrative: fresher data gives a tighter forecast.
inp.nudge: A quick update would sharpen your forecast.
inp.shareOn: On. De-identified entries only. Withdraw any time.
inp.persOn: On. Answers use your own history.
inp.persOff: Off. Answers use the library only.
inp.delAsk: Delete all data on this phone?
inp.deleted: Deleted. No copy exists anywhere else.
more: Schema-driven parsers read Apple Health exports (XML), Health Connect records and CSV or JSON files. Every row is checked for valid dates, units and ranges. Rows that fail are skipped and reported, never guessed.
Records are written to a local SQLite database, encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM. The key is derived on your phone with Argon2id.
Reminders are local notifications. Updating only adds new rows, and nothing already stored is sent anywhere.

val.title: Where we stand
val.lead: Technology should answer to the people who use it. Here's what that means for us, and what you can hold us to.

items.s: No feature, deadline or investor comes before the person using Trota.
d: We're building Trota because women deserve health tools that work for them: clear answers, a record they own, and nobody selling them anything along the way.
When a choice is hard, we ask one question first: is this good for the person on the other end? If it isn't, we don't ship it.

items.s: We share many of the worries about AI. At the same time, we don't think the answer is to look away.
d: Generative AI, as it's mostly being built today, has real costs. Much of it was trained on people's work without their consent. It uses a great deal of energy and water for data centres, which themseleves cause far more concern. It puts jobs and creative work under pressure, and it often treats personal data as raw material. Those costs land on people who were never asked.

We support strong, enforceable regulation. Companies shouldn't be left to mark their own homework. At the same time, AI is already inside the tools people use every day. If it's going to be there, someone has to show it can be built without compromising ethics.

So we use it for one job only: turning checked facts into plain sentences. It can't see what it doesn't need, it can't invent a source, and it never makes decisions about you. Machine learning may be tainted by the corporate world, we want to show that innovation doesn't have to come at the cost of our humanity and the lack of guardrails.

items.s: Your health is yours. So is the record of it.
d: Your records stay on your phone. Anything that could identify you is removed before a question leaves it, and backups are locked with a key only you hold. We can't hand over what we never have.
Sharing with research is off until you choose otherwise, and you can change your mind at any time. Nothing you type is used to train AI models.

items.s: Being heard shouldn't depend on how well you remember your own history.
d: Many women leave appointments feeling rushed or dismissed, unsure what to ask, with symptoms that are easy to brush aside when there's no record of them.
Trota helps you understand what's happening and walk in prepared, with a clear history you can show your doctor. It doesn't diagnose and it doesn't replace care. It helps you get better care.

items.s: Women's health has been studied too little, for too long. Fixing that shouldn't cost anyone their privacy.
d: For decades, medical research treated men as the default. Conditions that mostly affect women are still too often diagnosed late and funded less.
If Trota helps build the long-term data that's missing, it will be with consent, de-identified, open about how it's used, and drawn from women of every background, not only the easiest to reach.

val.holdT: What you can hold us to
val.holdD: Promises are easy to write. These are ones you can check.
pledges: We will never sell your data or show you ads.
Nothing you type will be used to train AI models.
Research sharing stays off unless you turn it on, and you can turn it off.
We'll publish what our library contains and how research data is used.
If something goes wrong, we'll tell you plainly and quickly.
Every decision about Trota has a person accountable for it, not a model.
val.close: No innovation is worth the loss of our humanity.

say.text: Ask [[anything]] about your body. Bring [[your data]] from the apps you already use. See [[where every answer comes from]]. And [[export it, pause it or delete it]] whenever you like.
